explain.say: Imagine your street has nowhere to fix bikes, so everyone walks. That is a problem, and also a chance! An entrepreneur is someone who starts a business to solve a problem. Look at the board: six steps from idea to business.

faq.a: An entrepreneur is someone who starts a business, taking a risk to turn an idea into a product or service people will pay for. The word comes from French for one who undertakes.
A business plan is a written plan saying what you will sell, who will buy it, what it will cost, what price you will charge and how you will find customers.
asks: How do I write a business plan?

faq.a: From their own savings, family and friends, bank loans, small microfinance loans, or investors who buy a share of the business. Some use crowdfunding, where many people give small amounts online.
asks: How do you fund a start-up?

faq.q: What happens if a business fails?
faq.a: The owner may lose money, but many successful entrepreneurs failed first and learned from it. Some countries have rules that let people close a failed business and start again.
asks: Is it bad if a business fails?

faq.a: Curiosity about problems, willingness to take sensible risks, listening to customers, careful planning, and the patience to keep going after setbacks.

facts: Infosys was founded in 1981 by seven engineers in Pune, India, with about 10,000 rupees.
The word entrepreneur comes from the French entreprendre, to undertake.
